question: In which Budget was Disinvestment Fund and Asset Management Company set up?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tue Apr 01 2003 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Disinvestment Fund and Asset Management Company were set up in the **Union Budget of 2003-04**.
 
• The primary goal of establishing the Disinvestment Fund was to channelize proceeds from the disinvestment of public sector enterprises (PSEs) for productive use.
 
• The Asset Management Company was introduced to professionally manage assets of public sector undertakings (PSUs) that were being disinvested.
 
• This step was in alignment with the Indian government's broader agenda of economic reforms and reducing the fiscal deficit.
 
• The initiative was overseen by the Ministry of Disinvestment, which was later merged with the Ministry of Finance in 2004.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disinvestment:**

 
 
• Disinvestment refers to the sale or liquidation of government-owned assets, typically public sector enterprises (PSEs).
 
• The objective is to reduce fiscal burden, improve operational efficiency, and encourage private sector participation.
 
• It also helps in raising funds for the government, which can be utilized for developmental or budgetary needs.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs):**
 
 
• PSUs are government-owned corporations where the majority stake (51% or more) is held by the central or state government.
 
• They are established to ensure that essential goods and services are available to citizens at affordable costs.
 
• Examples include Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) and Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**
 
 
• It occurs when the government's total expenditure exceeds its total revenue, excluding borrowings.
 
• Reducing the fiscal deficit is essential for maintaining macroeconomic stability and ensuring sustainable growth.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• Economic reforms in India, initiated in 1991, include liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG model).
 
• Disinvestment of PSEs is a crucial aspect of these reforms, aimed at reducing government control over industries and fostering competition.
